problems.field: assignment.randomized; support for the claimed criterion 1 conclusion
problems.source_says: The paper describes three between-participant feedback conditions but explicitly randomizes only the sequence of design problems. Neither the full text, Figure 2, nor the included supplement states that people were randomly allocated to Study 1 feedback conditions. Even accepting its numerical GPT-3 feedback as generative-model assistance, random condition assignment is unconfirmed. The current form correctly says not_stated; this is a barrier to the affirmative conclusion in the brief, not a newly identified error in that form. Attempts to retrieve the linked AsPredicted preregistration and the OSF project through Python urllib both failed with WinError 10013, so neither supplied additional evidence.
problems.quote: All three design problems were then administered in a random sequence.
problems.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 9), Procedure, lines 180-191, especially 188-189; PDF p. 12, Figure 2, inspected visually; entire included supplement, PDF pp. 39-52. Linked sources: https://aspredicted.org/bgmj-yrm4.pdf and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/6k52d/?view_only=398df4fd924440ee9387af4f6434d422 (retrieval attempts failed).

problems.field: ai_tool.name_model; arms[].ai; generative-AI requirement of criterion 1
problems.source_says: Random assignment is explicit, but it concerns the timing of originality-score feedback from AuDrA, a convolutional neural network trained to evaluate drawings. Participants draw their own images; the intervention is not an image generator or an identified generative language model. Page 13 inconsistently calls the scorer a fine-tuned large language model, but the named AuDrA system and explicit convolutional-network descriptions on pages 6 and 29 support the form's other_aid classification. Thus this randomized study does not establish random assignment to generative-AI assistance. The current form already records that limitation correctly.
problems.quote: Likewise, in Study 2, we used a convolutional neural network that was previously trained to evaluate creativity of line drawings
problems.locator: PDF p. 29 (printed p. 27), Discussion, lines 600-601; PDF p. 6, lines 78-81; PDF p. 13, Development of AI feedback, lines 224-234; random assignment on PDF p. 14, lines 249-251; numerical-only feedback on PDF p. 31, lines 644-647; creativity-codebook.md sections 1 and 3.

confirmed.statement: S1 uses a fine-tuned GPT-3 davinci-002 language model to score participants' own design solutions and return numerical originality feedback.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 7), lines 154-163; PDF p. 10, lines 164-169; PDF p. 40 (supplement printed p. 8), first supporting-text paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1 compares continuous feedback during practice and trials, feedback during practice only, and no feedback at any stage; all arms receive repeated be-creative prompts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 9), Procedure, lines 180-191; PDF p. 12, Figure 2 and caption.

confirmed.statement: S2 explicitly randomly assigns individual participants after warm-up to immediate or delayed feedback.
S2 reports 18,998 participants assigned to immediate feedback and 18,825 to delayed feedback, with 18,136 and 18,062 respectively in the cleaned dataset.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), lines 262-263; PDF p. 16 (printed p. 14), Data cleaning, lines 298-301.

confirmed.statement: S2 feedback concerns participants' own drawings and can precede their next drawing; the manipulation is not merely whose output evaluators judge.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), lines 224-234; PDF p. 17 (printed p. 15), lines 319-324; PDF p. 47 (supplement printed p. 15), Table S5 note.

confirmed.statement: For S2, both groups produce the first drawing without feedback; only the immediate group receives feedback before the second drawing, and both groups can receive feedback thereafter.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 17 (printed p. 15), Analysis strategy, lines 316-325; PDF p. 47, Table S5 note; PDF p. 12, Figure 2.

confirmed.statement: Both studies assign feedback schedules between participants. Repeated tasks or drawings do not establish a randomized crossover; the within-person condition-order criterion is not applicable to the coded designs.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 9), lines 180-191; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), lines 249-263; PDF p. 17 (printed p. 15), lines 312-325.

confirmed.statement: The feedback supplies numerical originality ratings only; qualitative explanations and suggested improvements are proposed as future work.
The supplement's random drawing selection and presentation concern human validation ratings, not assignment of creative participants to generative-AI assistance.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 40 (supplement printed p. 8), second supporting-text paragraph.

summary: The claimed randomized generative-AI conclusion is unsupported: Study 1's GPT-3 feedback has no stated random condition assignment, while randomized Study 2 uses the non-generative AuDrA scorer. The supplied form already records these limitations, and criterion 1 remains unclear.
